newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico creates 280,000 new jobs Jan-April - Werner.
newsitem.headline: Mexico creates 280,000 new jobs Jan-April - Werner.

text.p: Mexico has created 280,000 new jobs in the first four months of the year, Deputy Finance Minister Martin Werner said Friday.
Speaking on radio network Radio Red, Werner said in April the number insured via the Mexican Social Security Institute grew almost 103,000 workers.

"That takes us to a total of 280,000 jobs created in the January-April period," Werner said. "The figure is in line with the number of jobs that we want to create to absorb all the young people who join the working ranks year after year which is an increase close to one million (per year)," he added.

He said new jobs were being created in industry and that the service industry was also starting to see more opportunities, especially in commerce. "Almost half (new jobs) are in industry and the other half in commerce," he said.
Werner said internal demand was beginning to grow and that was showing in the service sector. He said last year industry was one of the few sectors to see job growth.

"In these first four months, employment in the industrial sector grew 4.6 percent and in the service sector it grew 3.1 percent. We are seeing the recovery of services which reflects internal demand," he added.
On inflation, Werner said the 1.08 figure for April announced Thursday by the central bank was a third of the inflation that the country had in April 1996, when the figure was close to 3 percent.
"It is expected that inflation in the next months will be similar (to April) or it could even be a little less," he said, adding that the 15 percent central bank target for 1997 is achievable.
"We can be very close to this objective for annual inflation if the tendancy continues," he said.

But he rejected the notion that economic recovery could generate inflationary pressures. "Supply indicators are close to 98 percent in virtually all goods...we do not see any sector that could have pressured prices," he added.
